summary.text: Rhett Marques is a Republican member of the Alabama House of Representatives (District 91) since 2018 and a small-business owner, and the Republican nominee for Alabama's 2nd Congressional District. He won the August 11, 2026 special Republican primary with 50.3% of the vote, and he serves as Vice Chair of the state House Commerce and Small Business Committee.

paragraphs.text: Marques was born and raised in Spanish Fort, Alabama, in Baldwin County. He graduated from Fairhope High School in 1990 and earned a marketing degree from the University of Alabama in 1994.

He owned and managed Goodson Tire & Auto in Enterprise, and Yellowhammer News reported in 2025 that he lives in the Wiregrass region and raised his two daughters in Coffee County with his wife, Christina.

Marques won the Republican primary runoff for Alabama House District 91 over Lister Reeves Jr. in 2018, succeeding Barry Moore in the seat representing Coffee County, and took office on November 7, 2018. He was re-elected in 2022.

In the legislature he has served on the Commerce and Small Business Committee, as Vice Chair since 2023, and on the Health Committee since 2019; his 2025-2026 assignments also include Transportation, Utilities and Infrastructure. He is not running for re-election to the state House in 2026.

Marques advanced from the May 19, 2026 Republican primary in Alabama's 1st District, but those results were voided and new primaries were held August 11 after federal courts allowed the state to use previously barred congressional maps.

Running in the 2nd District, he won the August 11 special Republican primary with 50.3% (15,468 votes), ahead of Hampton Harris (20.4%). 1819 News reported that he received endorsements from President Trump and U.S. Sen. Katie Britt.
